title: Union Carbide Corp. v. Oscar Mayer Foods Corp.
shortTitle: Union Carbide Corp. v. Oscar Mayer Foods Corp.
summary: Unexpected back-tax liability illustrates a materially altering allocation distinct from Bayway’s transaction-specific tax.
notes: The seller directed orders through an out-of-city address to avoid a tax. After authorities assessed approximately $88,000 in back taxes, it invoked a printed indemnity against the buyer. The reported judgment excluded the clause as material. Posner’s discussion treats hardship as a consequence rather than an independent criterion. Bayway quotes that skepticism but leaves the independent-ground issue undecided in its own case.

sources.label: Farnsworth et al., Contracts: Cases and Materials, 10th ed. (2023), pp. 289–290. Open assigned page 289.
